_comment: body_zone (head | chest | abdomen | arm | body) is a UI DESIGN decision, not medical: it only chooses where the indicator is anchored on the status board body figure ('body' = whole body / general); an indicator without body_zone is not shown on the figure. icon (heart | gauge | drop | thermometer | moon | smile | pulse) is the status board card icon, also a UI design choice. Ranges contain only cut-offs explicit in the cited sources. Edges are inclusive unless a range sets min_exclusive / max_exclusive (e.g. '<70' is max 70 with max_exclusive true). Consecutive numeric ranges must touch exactly with exactly one exclusive edge (the loader checks it); a gap is an error unless the indicator sets "allow_gaps": true, an explicit decision that the stretch evaluates to 'unknown' because the source does not define it. An empty range (min and max null) means the sources do not define it. Action texts may use {unit}, {range.<status>.min|max} and {range2.<status>.min|max} (ranges_secondary); they resolve from the effective ranges, so a threshold lives in one place. Numbers that are not range edges (e.g. the 15 g of the 15-15 rule) stay literal and keep their source. input.min / input.max / input.step are input plausibility limits, a design parameter of the form and not a medical threshold. Escalation levels (self/crew/ground) and protocol_id are DESIGN decisions, not medical. Every indicator stays PLACEHOLDER while any of frequency, how_to_measure or the actions has an unsourced part.

indicators.name: Heart rate

input._comment: input plausibility limits, design parameter, not a medical threshold

how_to_measure: To take a pulse at the wrist, place the index and middle fingers on the underside of the opposite wrist, below the base of the thumb.
To take a pulse at the neck, place the fingers beside the Adam's apple. Do not press on both sides of the neck at the same time.
Count the beats for 60 seconds, or count for 30 seconds and multiply by 2, for 15 seconds and multiply by 4, or for 10 seconds and multiply by 6.
indicators.why_it_matters: NASA's Human Research Program studies how spaceflight hazards affect the human body; tracking your resting pulse over time helps you notice changes.

text: Resting pulse is within the {range.normal.min} to {range.normal.max} {unit} reported for adults.
Resting pulse is outside the {range.normal.min} to {range.normal.max} {unit} reported for adults. Well-trained athletes can have a resting pulse of 40 to 60.
Contact a health care professional if it is consistently high or low at rest, the pulse is bounding for more than a few minutes, it is irregular, or it is hard to find.
PLACEHOLDER: the sources define no critical pulse threshold.

indicators.name: Blood pressure

input._comment: input plausibility limits, design parameter, not a medical threshold. second_lower_than_first: diastolic must be lower than systolic.

how_to_measure: PLACEHOLDER: step 1 of the measurement instructions for a non-expert.
indicators.why_it_matters: NASA's Human Research Program studies how spaceflight hazards affect the human body; tracking your blood pressure over time helps you notice changes.

text: Reading is in the normal category: below {range.normal.max} systolic and below {range2.normal.max} diastolic.
Reading falls in the elevated, stage 1 or stage 2 hypertension categories (systolic {range.attention.min} or higher, or diastolic {range2.attention.min} or higher).
PLACEHOLDER: what to do for elevated to stage 2 readings.
Severe hypertension: systolic above {range.critical.min} and/or diastolic above {range2.critical.min}. Contact a health care professional (here: ground control).

If there are symptoms such as chest pain, shortness of breath, back pain, numbness, weakness, change in vision or difficulty speaking, treat it as a hypertensive emergency and seek emergency help immediately.

text: PLACEHOLDER: the sources define only low blood sugar, not a normal or high range.
Low blood sugar (below {range.attention.max} {unit}). Follow the 15-15 rule: eat or drink 15 g of carbohydrate, wait 15 minutes, then recheck.
If it is still below {range.attention.max} {unit}, repeat. Once it is back in range, eat a balanced snack.
Severe low blood sugar (below {range.critical.max} {unit}). The person may faint and need help from others.
Glucagon and emergency care are needed.
